# Attribura iOS SDK — LLM integration guide

> Paste this whole file into your AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, …) and ask it to add
> Attribura self-report attribution — and, optionally, onboarding funnel tracking — to
> your iOS app. It is complete and self-contained.

## What this SDK does

Attribura measures which content drives real revenue. Deterministic tracking links cover
tapped traffic, but they miss two things: **dark social** (a friend showed someone the
app) and **App Store Search** (someone sees a Reel, then searches the app by name — Apple
logs it as Search, not your campaign). The SDK closes that gap: it captures the answer to
an in-app *"How did you hear about us?"* question and sends it to Attribura, which
correlates the reported channel with the content you posted.

- The SDK is **headless** — it ships NO UI. The app developer builds the onboarding step
  / bottom sheet and calls the SDK when the user picks an answer.
- It is **fire-and-forget**, thread-safe, has **zero third-party dependencies**, and
  buffers a failed send to disk to retry on the next launch.
- Attribution is **confidence-scored, never deterministic** — a self-report never
  overrides a certified link.

It optionally also records **which onboarding steps each run reached**. That second job is
only worth doing because of the first: a drop-off funnel on its own is a commodity, but
this one is joined to the channel the same run self-reported, so you can pull
*"TikTok installs drop at the notification step, Instagram installs don't"* — a split no
general analytics tool can make, because it never asked the question. Read it back with
the `get_onboarding_funnel` MCP tool or the matching data API endpoint.

Requirements: iOS 13+, Swift 5.9+.

## Install (Swift Package Manager)

Xcode → File → Add Package Dependencies… → `https://github.com/martindochamp/attribura-ios`
(Up to Next Major Version, from 0.2.1). Or in Package.swift:

```swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/martindochamp/attribura-ios", from: "0.2.1")
```

Then add `"Attribura"` to your target's dependencies and `import Attribura`.

## The entire public API

```swift
// Configure once, as early as possible. `token` is the org ingest token from the
// Attribura dashboard (Settings → Integrations → Attribura SDK). Optionally pass a
// default userId. `onboarding` declares your onboarding screens IN ORDER and is only
// needed if you want the funnel. Also flushes events buffered from a previous launch.
Attribura.configure(token: String, baseURL: URL, userId: String? = nil,
                    onboarding: [String] = [])

// Update the default user id later (e.g. after sign-in). Attaches the id to the WHOLE
// current onboarding run, including steps recorded before sign-in.
Attribura.setUserId(_ userId: String?)

// Mark that this run reached an onboarding step. The name must be one you declared in
// configure(onboarding:). Call it from onAppear / viewDidAppear of each screen.
Attribura.step(_ name: String)

// Start reporting purchases. Call once, right after configure. iOS 15+.
// Sends every StoreKit transaction exactly as Apple signed it; the server checks that
// signature against Apple's root before anything counts. Never calls finish().
Attribura.observePurchases()

// This install's anonymous id, and the same value as a UUID for StoreKit. Minted by the
// SDK (NOT identifierForVendor — that would make your app declare a Device ID), stored
// in a file in Application Support, gone when the app is deleted.
Attribura.anonymousId: String
Attribura.purchaseToken: UUID

// Start a NEW onboarding run. Only needed if one app session can onboard twice (e.g. a
// sign-out that returns the user to the start). Each run records a given step once.
Attribura.newRun()

// Report where a user heard about you. Fire-and-forget; safe on the main thread.
// No-op (asserts in debug) if called before configure.
Attribura.reportSource(_ source: AttributionSource,
                       userId: String? = nil,
                       prompt: String? = nil,
                       context: [String: String]? = nil)
```

### AttributionSource (enum)

Linkable channels (cross-checked against your recent certified-link posts):
`.instagram .tiktok .youtube .x .reddit .linkedin .threads .facebook`

Dark social (unlinkable, but the traffic every link misses):
`.googleSearch .appStoreSearch .friend .podcast .newsletter`

Anything else: `.other("Some Newsletter")` — free-text, lands in the dark-social bucket.

## Integration steps

1. Configure once at launch:

```swift
import Attribura

// e.g. in your App's init, or application(_:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:)
Attribura.configure(
    token: "atb_ingest_xxx",                              // from the dashboard
    baseURL: URL(string: "https://api.attribura.com")!
)
```

2. Report the money, so an answer becomes an amount. Two lines, and NOTHING to
   configure in App Store Connect:

```swift
Attribura.observePurchases()                       // once, right after configure

let result = try await product.purchase(           // on every purchase
    options: [.appAccountToken(Attribura.purchaseToken)]
)
```

   The `appAccountToken` is the whole trick: Apple stores it on the transaction and
   signs it, so the sale arrives already tied to the id that answered the question.
   Omit it and the sale is still recorded but belongs to nobody.

   Sandbox purchases are welcome — real signatures on fake money, kept apart so no
   revenue figure counts them. Use them to prove the chain before you ship.

   You do NOT have to unplug Superwall or Stripe first. Once an app reports Apple's own
   transactions, those are the ones that count, and the webhook stops crediting the same
   sale a second time — the direct road wins because Apple signs what it says.

2b. OPTIONAL — if your app has accounts, or if your paywall provider reports its own id
   (Superwall's `app_user_id`), pass it so both line up:

```swift
Attribura.setUserId(myAppUserId)   // once you know it (after sign-in)
```

3. Show your own "How did you hear about us?" step during onboarding, and call the SDK
   when the user answers (the SDK ships no UI — this sheet is yours):

```swift
import SwiftUI
import Attribura

struct HeardAboutUsSheet: View {
    let userId: String
    var onDone: () -> Void

    private let options: [(String, AttributionSource)] = [
        ("Instagram", .instagram), ("TikTok", .tiktok), ("YouTube", .youtube),
        ("A friend", .friend), ("A podcast", .podcast), ("App Store search", .appStoreSearch),
    ]

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 12) {
            Text("How did you hear about us?").font(.title3.bold())
            ForEach(options, id: \.0) { label, source in
                Button(label) {
                    Attribura.reportSource(source, userId: userId,
                                           prompt: "How did you hear about us?")
                    onDone()
                }
                .buttonStyle(.bordered)
            }
        }
        .padding()
    }
}
```

## Wire protocol (what the SDK sends)

The SDK POSTs to `{baseURL}/v1/ingest/self_report`, authenticating with the org ingest
token in the `X-Attribura-Token` header. You never call this directly — it's here so you
understand exactly what leaves the device. Example equivalent curl:

```
curl -X POST "https://api.attribura.com/v1/ingest/self_report" \
  -H "X-Attribura-Token: atb_ingest_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
        "source": "instagram",
        "user_id": "app-user-123",
        "prompt": "How did you hear about us?",
        "occurred_at": "2026-07-09T10:00:00Z",
        "platform": "ios",
        "sdk_version": "0.1.0"
      }'
```

Response:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "channel": "instagram",
  "attribution": {
    "method": "self_report_verified",
    "confidence": 0.6,
    "distribution_id": "…"
  }
}
```

Only `source` is required. `user_id`, `prompt`, `occurred_at`, `context`, `sdk_version`
are optional. The token is **write-only** — it cannot read data back.

When you track onboarding steps, the SDK also sends `run_id` (a per-launch id it mints in
memory) and `at_step` (the last step fired) on the self-report — those two are what let
the funnel be split by channel when you read it back.

Steps go to `{baseURL}/v1/ingest/steps`, **batched — one request per run**, not per step:

```
curl -X POST "https://api.attribura.com/v1/ingest/steps" \
  -H "X-Attribura-Token: atb_ingest_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
        "run_id": "6f1c…",
        "onboarding": ["welcome","goal","source","notifications","paywall"],
        "user_id": "app-user-123",
        "platform": "ios",
        "sdk_version": "0.2.1",
        "steps": [{"step": "welcome"}, {"step": "goal"}]
      }'
```

Steps are written to disk before they are sent, so an app killed mid-onboarding still
reports every step it reached. Resends are idempotent: a run records a given step once.
A step name you did not declare comes back in `undeclared` — a typo shows up here rather
than as a funnel row that looks wrong weeks later.

### Purchases

Transactions go to `{baseURL}/v1/ingest/storekit`, batched, as the JWS strings StoreKit
produced — nothing added, nothing parsed client-side:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.attribura.com/v1/ingest/storekit" \
  -H "X-Attribura-Token: atb_ingest_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"signed_transactions": ["eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NiIsIng1YyI6Wy..."]}'
```

The server verifies each one against Apple's root certificate before it becomes revenue,
and answers with what it did: `{"ok": true, "stored": 1, "duplicates": 0, "rejected": 0}`.
A transaction that fails verification is dropped and never fails the batch behind it.
Apple's `transactionId` is the idempotency key, so replaying a launch costs nothing.

## How attribution resolves (server side)

The reported answer is normalized to a channel and cross-checked against your recent
(last 30 days) certified-link posts:

- Exactly one recent post on that channel → `self_report_verified` (pins the exact post),
  confidence 0.6.
- Zero or several recent posts on a linkable channel → `self_report` (channel-level),
  confidence 0.45.
- A non-linkable answer (friend, podcast, App Store search, …) → `dark_social`,
  confidence 0.4.

A deterministic signal (the campaign token) always wins over self-report, so a
purchase that already carries a token is never overridden by a survey answer.

## Privacy & App Store

The SDK sends only what you pass (the answer + the user id) plus a timestamp and its own
version — no device identifiers, no advertising id (IDFA), nothing read back off the
device. It does **not** "track" in Apple's sense: it never links your users' data with
third-party data for ad targeting and shares nothing with data brokers — so it triggers
**no App Tracking Transparency (ATT) prompt**.

Two things to get right before you ship to the App Store:

1. The package ships a **privacy manifest** (`PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`) declaring what it
   collects: a **User ID**, one **Other** data type (the answer), and **Product
   Interaction** (the onboarding step names you declared) — all marked *linked to the
   user*, *not used for tracking*, purpose **Analytics**; `NSPrivacyTracking` is `false`.
   Xcode aggregates this into your app's privacy report automatically — you don't copy or
   configure anything. The onboarding run id is held in memory for the life of the
   process and never written to disk, which is why the manifest declares no
   required-reason APIs.
2. Reflect the same in **your app's** App Store privacy label (App Store Connect → App
   Privacy): a **User ID** and **Other Data**, used for **Analytics**, *linked to the
   user*, *not* used for tracking — plus **Product Interaction** if you call `step`, and
   **Purchase History** if you call `observePurchases`. If you already declare a user id
   for your revenue provider (Superwall/Stripe), you're most of the way there.
3. **No device or advertising identifiers.** `Attribura.anonymousId` is a UUID the SDK
   mints, deliberately not `identifierForVendor`, so you never have to declare a Device
   ID. It lives in a file in Application Support — not UserDefaults (a required-reason
   API) and not the Keychain (which would outlive the app). Deleting the app deletes it:
   a reinstall is a new person, and no ATT prompt is ever needed.

Since you pass the user id, keep your own privacy policy consistent with what you collect.

## Best practices

- Call `configure` once, as early as possible; it's cheap and flushes buffered answers.
- Ask the question ONCE per user, early in onboarding, before the paywall.
- Call `observePurchases()` and pass `.appAccountToken(Attribura.purchaseToken)` on every
  purchase — that pair is what turns an answer into attributed revenue, with no account
  and no permission prompt.
- If you also use Superwall or Stripe, pass the id THEY report via `setUserId` so both
  sides line up — and send purchases through one path only.
- Keep your own answer labels close to the enum cases; use `.other("…")` for the rest.
- RANDOMIZE the option order in your sheet per user (e.g. Swift `.shuffled()`). People who
  rush onboarding tend to tap the same position every time; shuffling averages out that
  positional bias so your channel mix isn't skewed toward whatever you list first.
- It's fine to call `reportSource` on the main thread from a button action.
- If you track the funnel, ASK THE QUESTION EARLY. The funnel can only be split by channel
  from the step where the answer arrives downwards — a run that quits before it never
  reported a channel, so the screens above show a total and no breakdown. Every screen you
  move the question up lights one more step. The trade runs the other way too: asked on
  screen one, the question costs some completion. After one easy commitment and before
  your first real ask is the sweet spot.

## Testing

`swift test` — the package's tests use a mock URLProtocol (no network). To smoke-test end
to end, point `baseURL` at your API and confirm a row appears under the dashboard's
Self-reported panel.
